# What this book is {.unnumbered}

This book is the guide to **ISLA** (Invariant Slice Attention), a neural
surrogate for steady, boundary-driven PDE problems. Given a discretized
boundary and the problem's global conditions, ISLA predicts the steady field
on that boundary and in the domain it bounds. The book is written the way a
user guide for a design code is written. It teaches what the method computes
and why each part is there. It shows how to run it. Then it lays out, with
the same care, what the measurements say for it and against it. The reader
we have in mind is fluent in PDE numerics and machine learning and has never
seen this program. Every term is defined where it first appears. Every
number is computed from a checked-in artifact as the page renders.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Where the name comes from"}
An *isla* is an island, a shape defined entirely by its boundary. The boundary is what the method takes as input.
The code class is `physicsnemo.experimental.models.ISLA`.
:::

## The thesis {#sec-verdict}

**ISLA is built around two invariances that no other slice-attention
surrogate has, rigid-motion equivariance, which is exact, and consistency
under a change of boundary discretization, which holds in the fine-mesh
limit, and at its reference configuration it is more
accurate than GeoTransolver at the recipe width on the DrivAerML Surface
task in less memory.** The comparison is against GeoTransolver, the
strongest published slice-attention surrogate, and Transolver. Every model
receives the same inputs and is scored on the same instrument at the
reporting protocol (@sec-protocol). The standing is this. On the DrivAerML
Surface task ISLA leads GeoTransolver-256 by 7% at full data and from 109
training cars up, in 0.7x its memory. The parameter-matched
GeoTransolver-512 is at parity, at 1.9x ISLA's memory and 1.17x its step
time. Below 109 cars GeoTransolver leads. On the HiLiftAeroML 35-wing rung
GeoTransolver and Transolver both lead by a quarter. Where the evaluation
departs from the training conventions, in pose or in how the surface is
sampled, ISLA's error barely moves, and the error of GeoTransolver and
Transolver grows by factors. ISLA and GeoTransolver reach the same accuracy
floor on the DrivAerML Surface task, ISLA at half GeoTransolver's
parameters. On the boundary-to-interior tasks ISLA leads
GeoTransolver-volume on velocity on both datasets and on pressure on the
cars. It trails on pressure on the airfoils. On the solids ISLA leads
GeoTransolver-512 on the lug. It trails on Tensile2d at 400 cases but has
the steeper learning curve. On the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set it trails by
a constant factor of three with the same learning-curve exponent. That is
the one dataset where ISLA's curve is not steeper. @tbl-thesis carries the
numbers, one row per dataset and task. Each row's chapter carries the
study behind it.

```{python}
#| label: setup-index
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean

# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 x 12, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4): results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
refm = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["mean"]
# DrivAerML Surface task, 435 cars, the reporting protocol: GeoTransolver-256 and Transolver at their better learning rate
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
isla200 = refm("isla_r1|dr435"); t200 = P2["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"]; gt512 = refm("gt_w512|dr435")
_gts = {k: P2[k]["pressure_mean"] for k in ("gt_unit_lr1e3", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if P2[k]["pressure_mean"]}
gt200_key = min(_gts, key=_gts.get); gt200 = _gts[gt200_key]; gt200_lab = "3e-3" if gt200_key.endswith("3e3") else "1e-3"
CSW = {r["arm"]: r for r in J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"] if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
memx = lambda a: CSW[a]["peak_allocated_gib"] / CSW["isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"]["peak_allocated_gib"]
# DrivAerML Surface task, the training-car ladder at the reporting protocol (the reference configuration's re-run)
RBS = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
lad200 = {n: min(RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"]["mean"], RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]["mean"]) / RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["mean"] for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
# HiLiftAeroML 35-wing rung at the reporting protocol: the reference configuration; the baselines from the fleet reduction
W35 = refm("isla_r1|hl35")
FL35 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json")["datasets"]["highlift_surface_super_scarce"]["arms"]
gt35 = FL35["gt_unit"]["pressure_l2_mean"]; t35 = FL35["transolver_unit"]["pressure_l2_mean"]
# the solids and the fixed-mesh boundary-data sets, GeoTransolver-512 (the parameter match) ÷ ISLA
LUGR = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json")["gt512_over_isla"]
lug = {300: LUGR["isla_r1_lr25e4|n300"], 600: LUGR["isla_r1|n600"], 1200: LUGR["isla_r1|n1200"], 2400: LUGR["isla_r1|n2400"]}
_LM = J("lane_means_2026-09-23.json"); _SFG = J("solids_frame_2026-09-22.json")["summary"]["gt512|gt|n400"]["fields"]
T2 = {f: _SFG[f]["mean"] / statistics.mean(_LM[f"v2_t2d_isla_r1_tensor_axis_n400_seed{s}"]["fields"][f] for s in (42, 43)) for f in ("sig11", "sig22", "sig12", "displacement")}  # tensor head + load axis, 400 cases
OLJ = J("olbc_2026-09-22.json"); olbc = {n: OLJ["gt512_over_isla"][f"poisson|isla_r1|n{n}"]["u"] for n in (512, 2048, 8448)}
olbc_x = (OLJ["learning_curve_exponents"]["poisson|isla_r1|u"]["exponent"], OLJ["learning_curve_exponents"]["poisson|gt512|u"]["exponent"])
JBR = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json")["gt512_over_isla"]; JBS = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json")["summary"]
jb_full = {f: JBS["gt256|full"]["fields"][f]["mean"] / JBS["isla_r1|full"]["fields"][f]["mean"] for f in ("von_mises", "displacement")}
# every case in a random pose, DrivAerML Surface task at the reporting protocol
PP = J("p200k_pose_r1_2026-09-23.json")
pose200 = {"isla": PP["arms"]["isla"]["posed_over_native"], "gt": PP["arms"]["gt_unit"]["posed_over_native"], "t": PP["arms"]["transolver_unit"]["posed_over_native"]}
pose200_lead = {"gt": PP["verdict"]["gt_aug_posed_over_isla_posed"], "t": PP["verdict"]["t_aug_posed_over_isla_posed"]}
# training-law study: each model trained under the uniform and under the area-proportional sampling law,
# scored on the independent uniform draw (wings: 35 HiLiftAeroML cases at 200,000 cells; cars: 435 DrivAerML cars at 100,000 cells)
TA = J("trainarea_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]; TAD = J("trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]
MODELS = (("isla", "isla_ref"), ("gt_unit", "gt"), ("transolver_unit", "t"))
law = {ds: {m: A[f"{m}_area"]["mean"]["unif"] / A[f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]["unif"] for m, _ in MODELS} for ds, A in (("wings", TA), ("cars", TAD))}
# sampling consistency at 100,000 cells: the uniform-trained arm scored on the 10:1 front/back biased draw ÷ on the uniform draw (cars)
dens = {m: TAD[f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]["biased"] / TAD[f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]["unif"] for m, _ in MODELS}
# capacity on the DrivAerML Surface task: ISLA 384 wide x 24 layers at 200,000 cells; GeoTransolver's ladder at 100,000
RN = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]; CAPC = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
RP = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")["configurations"]
cap = {"isla24": dict(RN["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"], pressure_l2_mean=RP["cars|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4|c200k"]["pressure_l2_mean"]),
       "gt1024": CAPC["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"], "gt2048": RN["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]}
M = lambda c: f"{c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M"
# DrivAerML Volume task: ISLA (reference configuration, 5e-4) against GeoTransolver-volume, 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 queries
VG = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]["gt_vol_unit"]
FIELDS = ("pressure_l2", "velocity_l2", "nut_l2")
vol_isla = {f: refm("isla_r1|drvol", f) for f in FIELDS}; vol_gt = {f: VG[f]["mean"] for f in FIELDS}
vol_ratio = {f: vol_gt[f] / vol_isla[f] for f in FIELDS}
# AirfRANS interior task: ISLA (reference configuration) against GeoTransolver-volume, 800 training airfoils, 100,000 queries per case
AF = J("airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json")
af_isla = {f: refm("isla_r1|af", f) for f in FIELDS}; af_gt = {f: AF["arms"]["gt_volume_1e-3"][f]["mean"] for f in FIELDS}
af_ratio = {f: af_gt[f] / af_isla[f] for f in FIELDS}
AFX = J("airfrans_extrap_2026-09-22.json")["splits"]
afx_split = {sp: {f: AFX[sp]["gt_over_isla_on_split"][f]["mean"] for f in FIELDS} for sp in ("reynolds", "aoa")}
afx_growth = {sp: {f: AFX[sp]["growth"][f]["g_gt_over_g_isla"] for f in FIELDS} for sp in ("reynolds", "aoa")}

def standing(r, names=("pressure", "velocity", "eddy viscosity")):
    """Word a triple of baseline ÷ ISLA ratios: above 1.02 ISLA leads, below 0.98 it trails, else level."""
    lead = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if r[f] > 1.02]; trail = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if r[f] < 0.98]
    level = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if 0.98 <= r[f] <= 1.02]
    parts = []
    if lead: parts.append("ISLA leads on " + " and ".join(lead))
    if trail: parts.append("trails on " + " and ".join(trail))
    if level: parts.append("level on " + " and ".join(level))
    return "; ".join(parts)
```

## Names, symbols and colors {#sec-key}

**Every thing in this book has one name and every architecture one
color.** The names below are canonical. Their definitions are in the
chapters cited.

| Name | What it is | Where defined |
|---|---|---|
| **ISLA** | the model as shipped, named without qualifier: the relative frame, the RMS-pairwise-distance length unit, cosine routing, the class defaults | @sec-isla, @sec-using-config |
| **ablation**, **diagnostic** | a configuration measured only to price a design choice (weights-off, raw coordinates, linear routing); never adopted | @sec-principled-decisions |
| **GeoTransolver**, **Transolver**, **GeoTransolver-volume** | the public slice-attention baselines, named without qualifier and never modified. "GeoTransolver + ISLA's *feature* (ablation)" is a baseline with one of ISLA's features added to isolate an effect; it is not a variant of the public model | @sec-baselines |
| **DrivAerML Surface task**, **DrivAerML Volume task** | the two tasks on the car dataset: surface pressure and wall shear at the boundary cells; pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity at interior queries from the boundary alone | @sec-datasets |
| **HiLiftAeroML, the $n$-wing rung** | the wing dataset, and one training-set size on its data-efficiency ladder ("the 35-wing rung") | @sec-datasets, @sec-data-efficiency |
| **AirfRANS interior task** | the airfoil dataset's boundary-to-interior task | @sec-datasets |
| **global vector inputs**, **global scalar inputs** | the problem's global conditions: $K$ unit directions $\hat g_k$ and $S$ scalars $\sigma$; on the benchmark instances $K = 1$, the far-field direction, and $S \in \{0, 1\}$ | @sec-pde-theory, @sec-isla-inputs |
| **measure weight** $w_i$ | the surface area a sampled cell stands for; the quadrature weight of every sum in the model | @sec-isla-quadrature |
| **relative frame** | ISLA's construction of position: no center, positions used only as differences to anchors, the measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the sample as length unit | @sec-isla-frame |
| **slice**, **anchor** | a soft group of tokens, and its measure-weighted mean position and normal | @sec-isla-slices |
| **relational invariants** | the scalars that describe a token relative to an anchor | @sec-isla-relational |
| **contract** | a structural property asserted to roundoff in float64 as a unit test | @sec-fidelity-columns, @sec-isla-contracts |
| **the two invariances** | rigid-motion equivariance (a contract) and discretization consistency (an acceptance criterion) | @sec-invariances |
| **the four sampling draws** | uniform over cells, stratified, 10:1 front/back bias, area-proportional | @sec-sampling-laws |
| **area-weighted relative L2**, **float32 instrument** | the metric and the precision every reported number is scored at | @sec-metrics |
| **the reporting protocol** | 200,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, each architecture at its own best learning rate, two seeds | @sec-protocol |
| **deficit anatomy** | the decomposition of the in-distribution gap into measured parts | @sec-deficit-anatomy |

```{python}
#| label: fig-key
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The book's visual key: every style a figure in this book uses. Left
#|   column: each architecture keeps its hue, marker and line style in every
#|   figure (GeoTransolver-volume shares GeoTransolver's); an ablation is the
#|   same hue, lighter and hatched, with an open marker. Right column: the
#|   marks that modify a series. Small dots are individual seeds and the large
#|   mark is their mean; an open marker of an architecture's shape is the same
#|   configuration trained under the area-proportional sampling law; lighter
#|   tints of a hue are narrower models on a width ladder, darkest widest.
#|   Color is never the only cue: marker shape and line style carry the same
#|   distinction. How to read this: the key defines styles, not results; no
#|   position in it means anything.
#| code-fold: true
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.6, 3.0))
# left column: architectures and their ablations
left = [("isla_ref", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver, GeoTransolver-volume"), ("t", "Transolver"),
        ("isla_abl", STYLE["isla_abl"]["label"]), ("gt_var", STYLE["gt_var"]["label"]), ("t_var", STYLE["t_var"]["label"])]
for i, (k, text) in enumerate(left):
    y = -i; x0 = 0.02
    kw = series_kwargs(k, lw=2.0, ms=8)
    ax.plot([x0, x0 + 0.06], [y, y], **{a: kw[a] for a in ("color", "ls", "lw")})
    ax.plot([x0 + 0.03], [y], marker=kw["marker"], ms=8, mfc=kw["mfc"], mec=kw["mec"], mew=1.8, ls="none", color=kw["color"])
    if STYLE[k]["hatch"]:
        ax.add_patch(mpl.patches.Rectangle((x0 + 0.075, y - 0.3), 0.025, 0.6, **bar_kwargs(k)))
    ax.text(x0 + 0.115, y, text, va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
# right column: modifiers, drawn on ISLA's hue but applying to every architecture
xr = 0.56
ax.plot([xr + 0.03], [0], marker="s", ms=7, color=BLUE, ls="none"); ax.plot([xr + 0.03] * 2, [0.33, -0.36], marker="o", ms=3.5, color=BLUE, ls="none")
ax.text(xr + 0.115, 0, "seeds (small dots); the large mark is their mean", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.plot([xr + 0.03], [-1], marker="s", ms=8, color=BLUE, mfc="white", mec=BLUE, mew=1.8, ls="none")
ax.text(xr + 0.115, -1, "open marker: trained under the area-proportional law", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
for j, (col, lab) in enumerate(((BLUE_PALE, "narrow"), (BLUE_LIGHT, ""), (BLUE, "wide"))):
    ax.plot([xr + 0.005 + 0.025 * j], [-2], marker="s", ms=8, color=col, ls="none")
ax.text(xr + 0.115, -2, "width shades: lighter is narrower, darkest is widest", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.plot([xr, xr + 0.06], [-3, -3], color=BLUE, ls=":", lw=2.0)
ax.plot([xr + 0.03], [-3], marker="D", ms=7, color=BLUE, mfc="white", mec=BLUE, mew=1.8, ls="none")
ax.text(xr + 0.115, -3, "dotted line, open diamond: a second ladder of one architecture (depth), named in the legend", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(0, 1.05); ax.set_ylim(-5.6, 0.6)
clean_axes(ax); ax.set_aspect("auto")
plt.show()
```

Two conventions hold in every table and figure. **A ratio between
architectures is baseline error divided by ISLA error**, so a value above
one favors ISLA. **Every error is the area-weighted relative L2 of
@sec-metrics, scored in float32** on the final-epoch checkpoint. A few
within-architecture comparisons are scored in bfloat16, and their captions
say so. No bfloat16 number is compared across architectures.

## How to read this book {#sec-how-to-read}

**The book reads in order. Each chapter assumes only the ones before it.**

- **The problem and how we measure** (@sec-problem): the boundary-to-field
  operator and its general interface, taught on a two-dimensional airfoil
  whose exact solution we know, then the generalization axes, the metric
  and the instrument.
- **ISLA, one idea at a time** (@sec-isla): why each part of the
  architecture is there, from "a sum over cells should be an integral" to
  the equivariant output basis.
- **The two invariances ISLA is built for** (@sec-invariances): what
  rigid-motion equivariance and discretization consistency mean, what each
  buys, and how each is measured.
- **The ISLA forward pass** (@sec-architecture): the computation stage by
  stage, with every tensor shape and code identifier.
- **Baselines, datasets and the protocol** (@sec-baselines): GeoTransolver
  and Transolver, the datasets and splits, and the rules that make a
  comparison fair.
- **Using ISLA** (@sec-using): the reference configuration, the inputs, the
  commands, the sampler, checkpoints and cost.
- **Evidence.** Surface accuracy and data efficiency on the DrivAerML
  Surface task and HiLiftAeroML (@sec-surface). Discretization and pose
  (@sec-robustness-density). Capacity, scaling laws and cost
  (@sec-shared-floor). Boundary to interior on the DrivAerML Volume and
  AirfRANS interior tasks (@sec-interior).
- **Limits and directions** (@sec-limits), then **program status**
  (@sec-program-status), the one chapter with dates.
- **Appendices.** The design-decision ledger (@sec-principled-decisions)
  and the lab notebook (@sec-notebook): every preregistration, launch and
  verdict, including the failures, in the order they happened.

Optional depth sits in collapsed notes like the one at the top of this
page. The throughline reads completely with all of them closed.

## What this book does not claim {#sec-not-claimed}

**Each claim in this book has a scope, and the list below names what sits
outside it.**

- **Not that ISLA is more accurate in distribution in general.** Its 7%
  lead at full data on the DrivAerML Surface task is against GeoTransolver
  at its recipe width. At matched parameters (GeoTransolver-512) the two
  are at parity, and ISLA's gain is cost, not accuracy. Below 109 cars and
  on every HiLiftAeroML rung GeoTransolver leads (@sec-surface).
- **Not that equivariance is an accuracy edge in general.** A baseline
  trained in a canonical frame is exactly pose-invariant. ISLA's pose lead
  is against baselines that learn pose from augmentation, in random poses.
  What the contract buys beyond that is stated in @sec-pose.
- **Not that discretization consistency is an exact invariance.** It is a
  fine-mesh-limit property: ISLA's residual under a biased draw is
  quadrature variance that shrinks with cell count (@sec-principle,
  @sec-robustness-density).
- **Not that ISLA is indifferent to the training sampling law.** Its
  dependence is weak beside GeoTransolver and Transolver, whose errors
  change by factors. Why the cars show the larger dependence is an open
  question (@sec-training-law).
- **Not that the interior lead is unconditional.** It is on velocity on
  two datasets and on pressure on one. GeoTransolver-volume leads on
  pressure and eddy viscosity on AirfRANS (@sec-interior).
- **Not that either architecture extrapolates across a flow regime** or
  transfers zero-shot to a different vehicle family (@sec-limits-regime,
  @sec-limits-transfer).
- **Not that the HiLiftAeroML numbers are test-set numbers.** They are
  validation numbers on final-epoch checkpoints (@sec-limits-validation).
- **Not that ISLA's learning curve is always the steeper one.** It is on
  Tensile2d, on the lug and on AirfRANS pressure. On the DrivAerML Surface
  task the two architectures' exponents are the same within the fit. On
  the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set they are equal, with a constant
  three-fold gap (@sec-compute-allocation, @sec-interior-olbc).
- **Not that the solid and fixed-mesh standings are final.** The lug's
  largest rung, the OLBC extension and the DeepJEB equal-epoch companion
  each await seeds or lanes in flight (@sec-program-status).
